issue.title: Chat passthrough for a "deepseek"-named upstream: injected `reasoning_content` collides with the client's echoed `reasoning` — 400 "duplicate field \`reasoning\`
issue.body:
## TL;DR / 中文摘要

本地部署的 DeepSeek 引擎（serde 反序列化）把 `reasoning_content` 视为 `reasoning` 的同一字段（别名）。客户端（pi、dsh）会把它自己流式收到的思考以 `reasoning` 字段回传到历史消息里。而 magpie 对 host/model 含 "deepseek" 的 Chat 上游，在工具调用轮给这些消息**追加** `reasoning_content`（`withReasoningOnToolTurns`），却不删除原有的 `reasoning`。两条消息字段同现，服务端反序列化直接报：

```
400 {"code":"json_parse_error","message":"deepseek: Failed to deserialize the JSON body into the target type: messages[6]: duplicate field `reasoning` at line 1 column 70565","param":null,"type":"invalid_request_error"}
```

结果：**只要走 magpie 且模型发起工具调用，紧随其后的每一条请求必 400**；不经 magpie 直连则一切正常。

## Environment

- magpie 0.1.1307 (installed, Windows 11 x64); verified against source commit `b855cfee`
- Clients: `pi` (OpenAI Chat) and `dsh`; both process-local
- Upstream: **self-hosted local DeepSeek engine** ("DeepSeek-Flash", OpenAI Chat-compatible, host redacted; both `/v1/chat/completions`; endpoint types incl. openai/anthropic/responses)

## What happens

For a request relayed as Chat to an upstream whose host or model contains `deepseek` (`chatReplaysReasoning`), magpie adds `reasoning_content` to every assistant tool-call turn — and to the reply turns after tool results — via `withReasoningOnToolTurns` (`internal/gateway/chattidy.go`, called from the `provider.Chat` branch in `internal/gateway/gateway.go`).

The engine this client talks to **streams assistant thinking in `reasoning`** (not `reasoning_content`). The client therefore echoes earlier tool-call turns' thinking in `reasoning`. After magpie's injection those messages carry **both** fields, and the engine's serde rejects a message with both keys mapped to the same struct field:

```text
duplicate field `reasoning` at line 1 column …
```

Every request of such a turn fails, so the whole tool call loop breaks. Direct (no magpie) sends only one field and works.

## Behavior verified directly against the engine (bypassing magpie)

Same conversation, assistant turn with `tool_calls` + tool result, only the assistant fields differed:

| assistant message fields | result |
| --- | --- |
| `"reasoning": "…"` only | **200** |
| `"reasoning_content": "…"` only | **200** |
| both | **400** `duplicate field \`reasoning\`` (exact error above) |

## magpie-side evidence

While routing `pi` and `dsh` through magpie, magpie's own usage ledger shows the identical shape every time on this provider:

- `pi`: 200 (`stop: "tool_calls"`) → next request **400** (user-visible: `messages[9]`)
- `dsh`: 200 (`stop: "tool_calls"`) → next request **400**, retry **400** (user-visible: `messages[6]`)

All other turns (no tool call, `stop: "stop"`) succeed — they don't match `withReasoningOnToolTurns`' injection condition, so no field collision.

## Why I think it's on the magpie side

The replay rule exists because official API assumes a **DeepSeek-style upstream that wants `reasoning_content` back on tool turns**. This engine is a DeepSeek-model Chat API too, but it *names* the field `reasoning` (that's what it streams) and tolerates reading the thinking from either name alone — just not both at once. The injection therefore assumes the more common client shape (thinking absent, or echoed as `reasoning_content`) and leaves any client-echoed `reasoning` in place.

## Suggested fix (draft)

In `withReasoningOnToolTurns` (`internal/gateway/chattidy.go`), after taking the thinking text, **remove the fields it was taken from** before writing `reasoning_content`, so the thinking is carried exactly once:

```go
think := reasoningText(m)
if think == "" {
    think = noReasoning
}
// the thinking rode in `reasoning`/`reasoning_details`: they go, or an
// upstream that reads both into one field (`reasoning`, with
// `reasoning_content` an alias) takes the message apart instead
// ("duplicate field `reasoning`")
for _, f := range messageReasoning[1:] {
    delete(m, f)
}
m["reasoning_content"], _ = marshalPlain(think)
```

(And in the early-return branch where the message already has a non-empty `reasoning_content`, drop leftover `reasoning`/`reasoning_details` the same way, returning `true` when it changed.)

Note this is lossless for official-style upstreams: the thinking still reaches the model — just under the name they actually read — and a client that echoed thinking in `reasoning` stops producing a two-key message. Possibly the same collision exists on the Kimi path (`reasoningDetailsAsContent` keeps `reasoning` while adding `reasoning_content`); not checked.

## Related observation

A `codex` run routed to the same engine through `/v1/responses` also failed with 400s around the same time (a different shape — `input[…]-level errors, not this exact text). Didn't repro it; mentioning in case it's the same vector from the Responses side (`withReasoningText`).

## Workarounds tried

- No config switch found for the replay/injection (checked settings + providers).
- Renaming the model inside magpie (to a name without `deepseek`) risks breaking upstream model resolution; no alias mapping exists in `providers.json`.
- Removing the client's echoed `reasoning` client-side isn't configurable either (pi/dsh echo the field the engine itself streams).

So for now, bypassing magpie for this provider is the practical workaround.

## Source & environment

- #3165 (wmfan2002-cloud): Chat passthrough to a self-hosted DeepSeek-compatible engine whose serde reads `reasoning_content` as an alias of `reasoning`. magpie's tool-turn replay (`withReasoningOnToolTurns`, `internal/gateway/chattidy.go`, reached from the `provider.Chat` branch in `internal/gateway/gateway.go` when `chatReplaysReasoning` matches) adds `reasoning_content` beside the `reasoning` the client echoes back, and the engine turns every such request away with `400 messages[N]: duplicate field \`reasoning\``.
- Fixed at `f5b01574` (= current `main`), branch `hunt58-f-3165-reasoning-dup`, macOS arm64, Go 1.25. All checks run locally: magpie's own gateway test stack, the upstream an in-process `httptest` fake (`internal/gateway`'s `fake`), no network, no real accounts.

## Minimal repro

`TestChatToolTurnReasoningCarriedOnce` (new, `internal/gateway/chat_tool_reasoning_test.go`): a Chat request relayed as sent to a provider whose model contains `deepseek`, where the client echoes the engine's streamed thinking in `reasoning` — an assistant tool-call turn with `"reasoning":"Thinking about the time."` and no `reasoning_content`, a reply after the tool result likewise. The fake upstream refuses, as the issue's engine does, any message carrying both fields:

```text
400 after 1 calls: {"error":{"code":null,"message":"dsflash: deepseek: Failed to deserialize the JSON body into the target type: messages[1]: duplicate field `reasoning` at line 1 column 70565","param":null,"type":"invalid_request_error"}}
```

Without the fix that is the issue's failure: 200 on the turn that made the call, 400 on every request after it.

## Root cause

`withReasoningOnToolTurns` takes the turn's thinking with `reasoningText` (reasoning_content, else `reasoning`, else `reasoning_details`' text) and writes `reasoning_content`, but leaves the field the thinking rode in on in place. A serde that maps both names onto one struct field rejects the two-key message (`duplicate field \`reasoning\``), exactly as the issue's A/B table shows (either field alone 200, both 400). The early-return branch — a message with a `reasoning_content` of its own — left an echoed `reasoning` standing beside it the same way.

## Fix

- Injection branch: after taking the text, the fields it was taken from (`reasoning`, `reasoning_details` — `messageReasoning[1:]`) go, before `reasoning_content` is written. The thinking reaches the model exactly once, under the name the replay path reads; lossless for official-style upstreams.
- Early-return branch: a leftover `reasoning`/`reasoning_details` beside a message's own `reasoning_content` is dropped, and the message is reported changed only when something went.
- `docs/subsystems/gateway-routing.md`: "is copied in" → "moves in — carried once".
- `TestChatToolTurnWithoutReasoningRelayed`'s expectation updated to the single-field shape.

Sibling surfaces checked, not changed: `buildChat`'s replay branch (`chat.go`) builds those messages itself, so there is no client field to collide with; `withReasoningText` (`responses.go`, the Responses replay) fills a `reasoning` item's `content` and adds no second name; `reasoningDetailsAsContent` (Kimi) still keeps `reasoning` when it writes `reasoning_content` — the issue leaves Kimi's aliasing behavior unchecked ("not checked"), so that path stays as it is.

## Verification

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `TestChatToolTurnReasoningCarriedOnce` without the fix (ablation: `chattidy.go` back at `f5b01574`, test kept) | FAIL — the 400 `duplicate field \`reasoning\`` above |
| `TestChatToolTurnReasoningCarriedOnce` with the fix | PASS |
| `TestChatToolTurnWithoutReasoningRelayed`, `TestChatToolTurnWithoutReasoningNotForMistral`, `TestTranslatedToolTurnWithoutReasoning`, `TestReasoningReplayed` | PASS |
| `go test -tags nogui ./internal/gateway/` (whole package) | ok 329s |
| `gofmt -l` (changed files) | nothing |
| `go vet ./...` | clean (a pre-existing cgo warning in `internal/gui` only) |
| `GOOS=linux go vet -tags nogui ./...` / `GOOS=windows go vet -tags nogui ./...` | clean |
| `go build` / `GOOS=linux go build -tags nogui ./...` / `GOOS=windows go build -tags nogui ./...` | ok |

## Not verified

- Not tried against the reporter's engine or api.deepseek.com: the aliasing serde semantics come from the issue's A/B table and its exact error text, reproduced through a fake upstream built to the same semantics.
- The Responses-side shape the issue mentions in passing (`withReasoningText`, `input[…]`-level errors) was not reproduced; this change does not touch that path.
- Kimi's path (`reasoningDetailsAsContent` keeping `reasoning`): the same collision is conceivable if a Kimi upstream aliases the names; unchecked there, unchanged here.

**Attribution**: AI-written; I've read the whole diff and the tests pass. Please keep the author (`ggbdpq`) or add `Co-authored-by: ggbdpq <ggbdpq@gmail.com>`.

## Source & environment

- #3165 (wmfan2002-cloud): Chat passthrough to a self-hosted DeepSeek-compatible engine whose serde reads `reasoning_content` as an alias of `reasoning`. magpie's tool-turn replay (`withReasoningOnToolTurns`, `internal/gateway/chattidy.go`, reached from the `provider.Chat` branch in `internal/gateway/gateway.go` when `chatReplaysReasoning` matches) adds `reasoning_content` beside the `reasoning` the client echoes back, and the engine turns every such request away with `400 messages[N]: duplicate field \`reasoning\``.
- Fixed at `f5b01574` (= current `main`), branch `hunt58-f-3165-reasoning-dup`, macOS arm64, Go 1.25. All checks run locally: magpie's own gateway test stack, the upstream an in-process `httptest` fake (`internal/gateway`'s `fake`), no network, no real accounts.

## Minimal repro

`TestChatToolTurnReasoningCarriedOnce` (new, `internal/gateway/chat_tool_reasoning_test.go`): a Chat request relayed as sent to a provider whose model contains `deepseek`, where the client echoes the engine's streamed thinking in `reasoning` — an assistant tool-call turn with `"reasoning":"Thinking about the time."` and no `reasoning_content`, a reply after the tool result likewise. The fake upstream refuses, as the issue's engine does, any message carrying both fields:

```text
400 after 1 calls: {"error":{"code":null,"message":"dsflash: deepseek: Failed to deserialize the JSON body into the target type: messages[1]: duplicate field `reasoning` at line 1 column 70565","param":null,"type":"invalid_request_error"}}
```

Without the fix that is the issue's failure: 200 on the turn that made the call, 400 on every request after it.

## Root cause

`withReasoningOnToolTurns` takes the turn's thinking with `reasoningText` (reasoning_content, else `reasoning`, else `reasoning_details`' text) and writes `reasoning_content`, but leaves the field the thinking rode in on in place. A serde that maps both names onto one struct field rejects the two-key message (`duplicate field \`reasoning\``), exactly as the issue's A/B table shows (either field alone 200, both 400). The early-return branch — a message with a `reasoning_content` of its own — left an echoed `reasoning` standing beside it the same way.

## Fix

- Injection branch: after taking the text, the fields it was taken from (`reasoning`, `reasoning_details` — `messageReasoning[1:]`) go, before `reasoning_content` is written. The thinking reaches the model exactly once, under the name the replay path reads; lossless for official-style upstreams.
- Early-return branch: a leftover `reasoning`/`reasoning_details` beside a message's own `reasoning_content` is dropped, and the message is reported changed only when something went.
- `docs/subsystems/gateway-routing.md`: "is copied in" → "moves in — carried once".
- `TestChatToolTurnWithoutReasoningRelayed`'s expectation updated to the single-field shape.

Sibling surfaces checked, not changed: `buildChat`'s replay branch (`chat.go`) builds those messages itself, so there is no client field to collide with; `withReasoningText` (`responses.go`, the Responses replay) fills a `reasoning` item's `content` and adds no second name; `reasoningDetailsAsContent` (Kimi) still keeps `reasoning` when it writes `reasoning_content` — the issue leaves Kimi's aliasing behavior unchecked ("not checked"), so that path stays as it is.

issue.body:
## Summary

`withReasoningOnToolTurns` adds a `reasoning_content` key to an assistant message **without removing the `reasoning` key the client already sent**. For an upstream whose request schema treats `reasoning_content` as an alias of `reasoning`, the resulting body contains the same logical field twice and is rejected:

```
Failed to deserialize the JSON body into the target type: messages[2]: duplicate field `reasoning`
```

The client always sees `200` because a routing group fails over, so this is invisible except in the first attempt of every affected request.

## Environment

- magpie **v0.1.1273** (also still present on `main`, checked at `138188a`)
- Upstream: an internal vLLM-based server exposing an **OpenAI Chat Completions** endpoint (host redacted; it is a `vllm-frontend-rs` / Rust + serde frontend, `owned_by: vllm-frontend-rs`)
- Client: an OpenAI-Chat agent client that replays prior-turn thinking in the **`reasoning`** field (not `reasoning_content`) on assistant messages — a legal and fairly common shape
- Provider config is plain Chat: `{"baseAPI": "chat", "chat": "https://<host>/v1", "models": ["deepseek-v4.1-flash"]}`

## Why this upstream rejects it

That server declares `reasoning_content` as a **serde alias** of `reasoning`, so an assistant message may carry either name but not both. Verified by POSTing straight at the upstream (no magpie involved):

| assistant message sent | result |
|---|---|
| `{"reasoning": "A"}` + `tool_calls` | `200` |
| `{"reasoning_content": "A"}` + `tool_calls` | `200` |
| `{"reasoning": "A", "reasoning_content": "A"}` + `tool_calls` | **`400 duplicate field \`reasoning\``** |

So the duplicate is not the client's doing — the client sends one key.

## Root cause

`internal/gateway/chattidy.go`, `withReasoningOnToolTurns` (`main` @ `138188a`, lines 373–402), write at line 399:

```go
func withReasoningOnToolTurns(body []byte) []byte {
	afterTool := false
	return editMessages(body, []string{"tool_calls"}, func(m map[string]json.RawMessage) bool {
		...
		var own *string
		if decodeJSON(m["reasoning_content"], &own) == nil && own != nil {
			return false               // guarded on reasoning_content only
		}
		think := reasoningText(m)      // ...but reasoningText() READS `reasoning` first
		if think == "" {
			think = noReasoning
		}
		m["reasoning_content"], _ = marshalPlain(think)   // line 399: ADDS a second key
		return true
	})
}
```

The guard asks "does this message already have `reasoning_content`?" but `reasoningText` (`chattidy.go:330`, keyed on `messageReasoning = {"reasoning_content", "reasoning", "reasoning_details"}`, `chattidy.go:326`) happily sources the text from `reasoning`. When it does, line 399 copies the text into a **new** `reasoning_content` key while the original `reasoning` key stays on the message — the body now carries both.

Reached from `internal/gateway/gateway.go:4023`, gated by `chatReplaysReasoning` (`internal/gateway/chat.go:260`: host or model contains `deepseek`, or Command Code's plugin) — i.e. exactly the providers most likely to have a strict parser.

This is consistent with the function's own doc comment, which only ever considers `reasoning_content`:

```go
// A message with reasoning_content of its own keeps it, any other reply is
// left as it is (DeepSeek doesn't ask for its thinking)
```

## Repro

Client body (one key — what the agent actually sends):

```json
{"model": "deepseek-internal/deepseek-v4.1-flash", "max_tokens": 32,
 "messages": [
   {"role": "user", "content": "hi"},
   {"role": "assistant", "content": "ok", "reasoning": "A",
    "tool_calls": [{"id": "c1", "type": "function",
                    "function": {"name": "f", "arguments": "{}"}}]},
   {"role": "user", "content": "again"}]}
```

Against a running gateway:

```
POST /v1/chat/completions          -> 400
"deepseek-internal: Failed to deserialize the JSON body into the target type:
 messages[1]: duplicate field `reasoning` at line 1 column 222"
```

`messages[2]: duplicate field \`reasoning\`` in the wild, on a real captured agent request (see below).

A/B/C, all with the *same* body otherwise:

| variant | model | result |
|---|---|---|
| A | `deepseek-internal/deepseek-v4.1-flash` (direct member id) | **`400 duplicate field \`reasoning\``** |
| B | `group/flash` (routing group) | `200` — but served by a *different* member (the deepseek member's attempt 400'd and failed over) |
| C | A with the single key renamed `reasoning` → `reasoning_content` | `200` from the deepseek member |

> ⚠️ Note the asymmetry: a client that replays in `reasoning_content` never trips this (`own` is set, guard returns false), while a client that replays in the equally valid `reasoning` always does.

## Captured real-world request

I captured the exact body an OpenAI-Chat agent client emits, against a local mock, to be sure this is not a synthetic shape. The second (follow-up) request of a tool-using session contains:

```json
{"role": "assistant",
 "reasoning": "I should list the files first.",
 "tool_calls": [{"id": "call_abc123", "type": "function",
                 "function": {"name": "bash", "arguments": "{\"cmd\":\"ls\"}"}}]}
```

Replaying **that captured body verbatim** through the gateway:

- with `"model": "deepseek-internal/deepseek-v4.1-flash"` → `400 duplicate field \`reasoning\``
- with `"model": "group/flash"` → `200`, answered by a fallback member (`glm-5.3-flash`), not the deepseek member
- with only `reasoning` renamed to `reasoning_content` → `200` from the deepseek member

## Impact

Small but constant tax, and it hides real failures:

- Over one day's routing log: **`group/flash` made 6,983 requests, of which 879 (12.6%) spent their first attempt on this 400.** Every one was an agent request.
- Of the 9 members of that group, **only this one rejects the duplicate** — the other 8 have tolerant parsers and swallow it. So which member you land on decides whether it fires.
- With the member listed first in an `order`-routed group, the first attempt is wasted on nearly every tool-using follow-up.
- The client never learns: it sees `200` while the member it asked for refused.
- Because the fault is invisible at the client, it is easy to misattribute to the member's own provider config.

## Suggested fix

Drop the other spelling(s) before writing, e.g. in `withReasoningOnToolTurns`:

```go
think := reasoningText(m)
if think == "" {
    think = noReasoning
}
delete(m, "reasoning")
delete(m, "reasoning_details")
m["reasoning_content"], _ = marshalPlain(think)
```

or generally: when normalizing to one reasoning key, remove every other key in `messageReasoning` from the message so the body never carries two. `withoutMessageReasoning` (`chattidy.go`) / the `refusedInMessages` path deserve the same audit — any place that adds a reasoning spelling should first clear the alternatives.

Happy to send a PR if you prefer that route.

issue.body:
### Your current environment

vllm-openai 0.32.0


### 🐛 Describe the bug

## Summary

With the Rust frontend (`VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=1`), a chat request whose assistant message carries **both** `reasoning` and `reasoning_content` is rejected with:

```json
400 {"error":{"message":"Failed to deserialize the JSON body into the target type: messages[2]: duplicate field `reasoning` at line 1 column 44919","type":"invalid_request_error","param":null,"code":"json_parse_error"}}
```

The Rust request schema declares `reasoning_content` as a serde alias of `reasoning`, and serde's default behavior rejects two keys mapping to the same struct field. The Python frontend (Pydantic) silently accepts both keys — duplicate JSON object keys are last-wins in Python's `json`, and `reasoning_content` is normalized to `reasoning` before rendering (`_normalize_messages_before`, #42664). So an identical body returns **200 on the Python frontend and 400 on the Rust frontend**.

This is a behavior regression for clients when switching to the Rust backend, and it hard-breaks multi-turn agent loops: the offending assistant turn stays in the conversation history, so **every subsequent request fails too**, and harnesses that retry surface the failure to the user (see "Real-world impact").

## Context

- The Rust frontend (`vllm-rs`, `owned_by: vllm-frontend-rs`) is opt-in via `VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=1` since 0.29. Feature parity is tracked in #44280.
- The Python frontend has iterated on exactly this field family: #42664 normalized `reasoning_content` → `reasoning` on the chat path, PR #52513 extends the normalization to `/tokenize` and pooling chat endpoints, PR #41718 additionally *rejects* (at the semantic layer, with a clear error) messages that carry both a top-level `reasoning` and typed `thinking` blocks. The Rust frontend instead fails at the JSON *deserialization* layer: the request never reaches any normalization, and the error message (`duplicate field ... at line 1 column N`) is opaque to clients.
- Related client-side reports of this same server behavior (all confirm the collision fires server-side in the Rust frontend, independent of the intermediary):
  - https://github.com/yetone/magpie/issues/2607 — includes an A/B/C matrix showing `reasoning`-only and `reasoning_content`-only both return 200 against a `vllm-frontend-rs` upstream, while both keys together return the 400 above.
  - https://github.com/yetone/magpie/issues/3165 — same collision via a different injection path.
  - https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/136486 — same error text against a "serde/Rust frontend in front of a vLLM backend"; their self-healing layer can't learn the rejection because the message is a `json_parse_error`, not a semantic field rejection.

## Steps to reproduce

Serve any model with the Rust frontend enabled:

```bash
VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=1 vllm serve <model> 
```

Send an assistant history message carrying both spellings of the thinking field (this is what agent harnesses do when they replay a prior assistant turn: some emit `reasoning`, some `reasoning_content`, and some emit both after a proxy or the harness itself merges the two):

```bash
curl -s http://localhost:8000/v1/chat/completions \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "model": "<model>",
    "max_tokens": 32,
    "messages": [
      {"role": "user", "content": "hi"},
      {"role": "assistant", "content": "ok",
       "reasoning": "I should greet them.",
       "reasoning_content": "I should greet them."},
      {"role": "user", "content": "again"}
    ]
  }'
```

## Actual result

Rust frontend: `400` with `json_parse_error`:

```
Failed to deserialize the JSON body into the target type: messages[2]: duplicate field `reasoning` at line 1 column 44919
```

Verified matrix against the same running server (`/version` reports `owned_by: vllm-frontend-rs`):

| assistant message carries | Rust frontend | Python frontend |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `"reasoning": "A"` only | 200 | 200 |
| `"reasoning_content": "A"` only | 200 | 200 |
| both keys | **400 `duplicate field \`reasoning\``** | 200 |

## Expected result

Parity with the Python frontend: the request is accepted and the thinking is carried exactly once. At minimum, a message with both aliases should not be a hard `json_parse_error` before the request is even parsed.

## Real-world impact

Observed with agent harnesses that replay prior assistant thinking in the history:

- **VS Code Copilot agent harness** against our Rust-frontend deployment: multi-turn tool-using sessions fail on every follow-up request with the error above, surfaced to the user as "Sorry, your request failed. Please try again. ... Last error: 502 Request Failed: 400 {duplicate field `reasoning`...}" after 5 retries (the 400 is deterministic, so retries never help).
- The magpie gateway reports 12.6% of all agent requests through one routing group spent their first attempt on this 400 (magpie#2607).
- Because the offending message stays in history, the failure is **permanent for the session** once it occurs.

## Root cause (likely)

The chat message struct in the Rust frontend (under `rust/`, the `vllm-chat` crate's request types) uses something like:

```rust
#[serde(alias = "reasoning_content")]
pub reasoning: Option<String>,
```

serde's derived `Deserialize` treats every unknown key as a field candidate and raises `duplicate field` when a struct field receives two values — including via aliases. Python's Pydantic path instead normalizes the two names before use.

## Proposed fix

Any of these restores parity; 1 is the closest match to the Python behavior:

1. **Accept both, last-wins (or first non-null):** deserialize the message into a `serde_json::Value` (or an intermediate with separate `reasoning` / `reasoning_content` options) and merge in `From`, mirroring `_normalize_messages_before`. Deterministic and parity-preserving.
2. A custom `Deserialize` impl for the message type that consumes alias keys tolerantly instead of erroring.
3. At minimum, pre-normalize/strip duplicate keys before strict deserialization so the error, if any, becomes a *semantic* 400 with a actionable message (as PR #41718 does on the Python side) rather than an opaque `json_parse_error` at the parse layer.

Worth auditing adjacent cases with the same shape while in there: duplicate/alias pairs on other fields (e.g. `thinking` content blocks vs the top-level field, per #41718) currently produce equally opaque parse-layer failures.

## Environment

- vLLM: <!-- fill in, e.g. 0.29.x / current main --> with `VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=1`
- Client: VS Code Copilot agent harness (also reproduced via plain `curl`, and independently reported from magpie, Hermes Agent, and litellm-fronted deployments)
- Model: <!-- fill in -->

## Duplicate check

- Searched `vllm-project/vllm` for `duplicate field` + `reasoning` and Rust-frontend reasoning issues: no open issue reports this. #42664 / PR #52513 / PR #41718 cover the **Python** frontend's normalization only; #44280 (Rust frontend parity roadmap) does not list this item.
- The client-repo issues linked above confirm the rejection originates in the Rust frontend itself.

### Before submitting a new issue...

- [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

issue.title: [bug] Responses → Chat for Mistral: `deepseek-*` model gets `reasoning_content` echoed back → 422 extra_forbidden (Codex breaks after first tool call)

repository.name: magpie
repository.description: Every agent's model. One place. Codex on DeepSeek, Claude Code on Kimi, from the menu bar.

issue.body:
## Problem

Follow-up to #494 (fixed in 0.1.616 for the Chat passthrough). The Chat Completions route still works, but the
`/v1/responses → /v1/chat/completions` route (what Codex uses) sends an earlier assistant turn's reasoning to Mistral as
`reasoning_content` when the model name is DeepSeek-like. Mistral rejects it:

```text
Mistral10977752: 422 Unprocessable Entity: {"detail":[{"type":"extra_forbidden","loc":["body","messages",1,"assistant","reasoning_content"],"msg":"Extra inputs are not permitted","input":"I should read note.txt with the tool."}]}
```

In Codex the first request of a turn succeeds; every follow-up after a tool call fails with 422 (repeated, so the
"retry without the rejected field and remember it" fallback from #494 does not kick in on this route either).

## Environment

| Item | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Magpie | 0.1.2710 (Windows app) |
| Client | Codex Desktop 0.166.0-alpha.5.1 (`effort: max`) |
| Provider | `mistral` preset, `https://api.mistral.ai/v1` |
| Model | `deepseek-v4-1-flash-1017` |

## Reproduction

```sh
curl http://127.0.0.1:3425/v1/responses \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer magpie' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"<mistral-provider>/deepseek-v4-1-flash-1017","stream":false,"max_output_tokens":40,
       "tools":[{"type":"function","name":"read_file","parameters":{"type":"object","properties":{"path":{"type":"string"}}}}],
       "input":[
         {"type":"message","role":"user","content":[{"type":"input_text","text":"Read note.txt and tell me the word."}]},
         {"type":"reasoning","summary":[{"type":"summary_text","text":"I should read note.txt with the tool."}]},
         {"type":"function_call","call_id":"call_1","name":"read_file","arguments":"{\"path\":\"note.txt\"}"},
         {"type":"function_call_output","call_id":"call_1","output":"pelican"}]}'
```

| Request | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `/v1/responses`, `deepseek-v4-1-flash-1017` | **422** extra_forbidden `reasoning_content` |
| `/v1/responses`, `zai-glm-5-3` (same provider) | 200 |
| `/v1/responses`, `mistral-medium-latest` (same provider) | 200 |
| `/v1/chat/completions` with `reasoning_content` on an assistant turn, `deepseek-v4-1-flash-1017` | 200 |

So it looks like the DeepSeek "reasoning must be passed back" handling (keyed on the model name) re-adds
`reasoning_content` after the Mistral-specific conversion to a `thinking` content part, on the Responses route only.
Possibly the same name-keyed injection as #3165 / `withReasoningOnToolTurns` in #2607, but here the upstream is
Mistral, which rejects the field outright.

## Expected

For a Mistral upstream (preset or `api.mistral.ai` host), never send `reasoning_content` / `reasoning` /
`reasoning_details` as message fields regardless of the model name, same as the Chat route since 0.1.616.
